items.summary: Today your treasurer or office staff type every gift into ChurchCRM by hand — including gifts that already arrived through an outside giving tool. Online giving would let a member give by card or bank transfer and have the gift show up in ChurchCRM ready for deposits and year-end statements, with no re-typing. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how your church takes online gifts today.
items.title: Giving online through ChurchCRM

items.summary: Today staff text members from their personal phones, so messages are scattered and there is no record of who was reached. Texting from ChurchCRM would let staff send one message to a person, a group, or the whole congregation from a single place. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with what your church texts about most.
items.title: Send a text from ChurchCRM to people and groups

items.summary: Pastors and staff keep sensitive notes — hospital visits, care conversations, family situations — that not everyone should be able to read. Tell us which records your church needs to keep private and who should see them, so the access rules match how your staff actually work day to day.
items.title: Keep some family or note records private

items.summary: Today a member's pledge starts on a paper card that office staff type into ChurchCRM by hand, and after that the member can't see how their giving is tracking. Portal pledges would let a member record, change, and follow their own pledge in the Member Portal, beside their giving history. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how pledge season works at your church.
items.title: Make and track your pledge in the Member Portal

items.summary: Today an event's location is free text typed by hand, so the same room gets spelled three ways and two groups can book it at once without anyone noticing. Event places would let whoever creates an event pick from one shared list of your church's rooms and places. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how you track rooms today.
items.title: Pick a place for your event from a shared list

items.summary: Today your newsletter lives in a separate service with its own copy of everyone's email address, and the two lists drift apart as people join, leave, and change addresses. Newsletters would connect ChurchCRM to services like Mailchimp so the people and groups you already keep drive who receives each newsletter. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how you send yours.
items.title: Send church newsletters from ChurchCRM

items.summary: Today businesses, partner churches, and mission agencies get squeezed into family records, with household fields that don't fit and giving mixed in awkwardly. Organisations as contacts would give them their own record — name, address, key contact, notes, and giving — presented as an organisation everywhere. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how you track organisations today.
items.title: Keep organisations as contacts, not families

items.summary: Today giving can only be recorded against a family, so a person who gives on their own needs an artificial one-person family that clutters the directory and reports. Person-level giving would let donations and pledges belong to a person as well as a family, while household giving stays as it is. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with where family-only giving causes you trouble.
items.title: Track giving to a person, not only a family

items.summary: Today the flyer, registration form, and permission slip for an event live in Drive, Dropbox, or an email thread — anywhere but on the event itself. External resource links would attach labeled links to those files directly on events and other records, each visible only to the right audience: public, members, or staff. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with which documents you wish were attached.
items.title: Attach event files and forms stored elsewhere

items.summary: Today ChurchCRM tracks money in — giving, pledges, deposits — and has nowhere to record money out, so spending lives in spreadsheets and receipts live in shoeboxes. Expense management would add a simple expense register with categories, funds, receipts, and budget-vs-actual reporting. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how you track spending today.
items.title: Track what the church spends, not just what it receives

items.summary: Today a hospital visit or a bereavement follow-up leaves no structured trace — at most a free-text note — so nobody can see who was visited last or which follow-ups are still outstanding when a pastor is away. Visitation tracking would keep real visit records: who visited whom, when, why, and what is still owed, with the privacy these records need. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how your care team keeps track.
items.title: Keep a real record of pastoral visits

items.summary: Today baptisms, marriages, and funerals live in free-text notes or custom fields — a date with no officiant, witnesses, or place, and no register you can search or print. Lifecycle tracking would keep real register records for each milestone, with per-type register views and printing. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how your church keeps its registers.
items.title: Keep a register of baptisms, marriages, and funerals

items.summary: Today ChurchCRM can say who is in a group now, but not who served as elder in 2019 or whose terms end this year — that history lives in minute books and spreadsheets. Leadership history would record offices and terms over time, so service is kept instead of overwritten. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how you track terms at your church.
items.title: See who served as a leader, and when

items.summary: Today ChurchCRM assumes one congregation in one place, so a church with several campuses runs a separate install per site and splits the membership and reports that should be shared. Multi-campus support would give people, groups, events, and finances a campus dimension in one system. Vote if this should be built next, and comment with how your campuses work today.
items.title: Run one church across several campuses
